```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
dseams::dseams_threads(1L)
```

dseams reads a trajectory frame into the d-SEAMS engine and returns the
results as data frames. Three small dumps ship with the package:

```{r}
library(dseams)
dseams_example()
```

## A perfect crystal

`ice1h.lammpstrj` is a 2x2x2 ice Ih cell with 128 oxygen sites. Every
water is hexagonal ice under CHILL+, and the hydrogen-bond network is
made of six-membered rings only:

```{r}
ice1h <- read_frame(dseams_example("ice1h.lammpstrj"), type = -1L)
ice1h
table(chill_plus(ice1h)$name)
primitive_rings(ice1h, graph = "cutoff", max_depth = 6L)
```

## A mixed frame

`exampleTraj.lammpstrj` is one frame of a TIP4P system. Type 2 is oxygen.

```{r}
frame <- read_frame(dseams_example("exampleTraj.lammpstrj"), type = 2L)
ice <- chill_plus(frame)
table(ice$name)
table(chill_plus(frame, graph = "mutual")$name)
```

`graph = "cutoff"`, the default, is the distance list. `graph = "mutual"`
is the mutual four-neighbour list. On this dump the cutoff list gives 9
interClathrate and 241 water, and the mutual list gives 1 clathrate, 7
interClathrate, and 242 water.

The ring census and the Steinhardt parameters come back the same way:

```{r}
primitive_rings(frame, max_depth = 6L)
q3 <- steinhardt(frame, order_l = 3L)
summary(q3$ql)
```

Each result is a data.frame, so the usual subsetting works:

```{r}
head(ice[ice$name != "water", ])
```
